title: Binance users in some European countries told to pull crypto before fees kick in, with accounts closing by year end
content: Affected accounts are reportedly set to close on Dec. 31. Users in Spain, France, and Poland say they've received similar notices.

title: U.S. Treasury moves to cut off crypto exchange MEXC over $16 billion in alleged illicit flows
content: Treasury billed the move as part of its campaign against Iran, but the order rests on MEXC's alleged role in Russian illicit finance.

title: Gnosis Pay breach exposes card numbers, home addresses and linked crypto wallets
content: One user said the exposed data tied his home address and card number to every crypto wallet linked to his account, raising the risk of targeted scams.

title: Apple, Meta reject OKX–ICE tokenized stock plans, leaving crypto firms as the ones to watch
content: Strategy, Coinbase, Circle and Robinhood are among six companies from the venture’s initial selection with no disclosed objection, after 90% of issuers opted out.

title: U.S. prediction markets regulator issues demand that clashes directly with courts
content: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said regulated exchanges can't cut off customers state-by-state, but firms like Kalshi are under court orders to do so.

title: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto
content: Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard.

title: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it?
content: Bitcoin’s eCash fork gives eligible holders an equivalent balance of ECX, but questions remain over where they can trade the tokens and what they can do with them.

title: US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties
content: US also offers as much as $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program.

title: Suspicious prediction market activity seen before election poll release: NYT
content: Bets were placed shortly before two recent New York Times/Siena political polls were released to the public, according to a report.

title: Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
content: Apple and Meta’s objections mean all seven of the biggest U.S. tech companies have now asked to keep their shares off the planned OKX-ICE venue.

title: AI Chip Stocks Bounce After Global Rout—But Is the Bubble Starting to Burst?
content: A Friday rebound offered relief after a historic selloff. The question now is whether politics and mounting debt could turn an AI correction into something much worse.

title: Sony Axing Game Discs Will Have Outsized Impact on Low-Income Gamers, Experts Say
content: Experts say a disc-free PlayStation will price out low-income players, while in much of Africa, digital-only gaming means breaking Sony’s rules.

title: Treasury Cuts Crypto Exchange MEXC Off From US Financial System
content: FinCEN’s order, part of Operation Economic Outcast, bars U.S. institutions from any transfers to or from MEXC, which Treasury says facilitated $16 billion in illicit finance tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia.

title: Greece Passes Crypto Tax Law With 10% Gains Levy, 15% on Staking and DeFi
content: Greece has approved a crypto tax framework with a €500 ($557) annual gains threshold and new rules for staking and DeFi income, but lawmakers left important questions about token swaps unresolved.

title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
content: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows FinCEN issued a final order under section 9714(a) that will bar U.S. financial institutions from sending or receiving funds with MEXC Global 30 days after Federal Register publication, citing at least $16 billion in alleged illicit activity. This post U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

title: Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
content: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, pleaded guilty Thursday to wire fraud and money laundering after using wallet credentials from 35 FBI investigations to take about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency.
